question: Should OpenClaw accept default preservation plus explicit opt-in replay of locally modified packaged `dist` files, together with the exact inventory-less release compatibility list?
rationale: The implementation is coherent and well-proven, but it establishes a new updater policy for mutating executable package files and deciding which older packages bypass integrity metadata requirements.

options.title: Approve guarded replay
options.body: Accept preservation by default and `--reapply-local-overrides` after package/security review confirms the replay boundary and legacy exception list.

options.title: Preserve without replay
options.body: Keep recovery bundles, diagnostics, and content-inventory hardening while removing updater-driven reapplication of local edits.

options.title: Split integrity hardening
options.body: Land package inventory and tarball checks separately while deferring local override replay policy.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded replay
recommendation.body: Accept preservation by default and `--reapply-local-overrides` after package/security review confirms the replay boundary and legacy exception list.

likelyOwner.reason: The live assignment and updater history make `steipete` the strongest available owner for the package mutation and compatibility decision.
